column3: The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
The Hebrew repeats the Sabbath root as the land’s action and its Sabbath; BSB uses “observe a Sabbath.”
The Hebrew repeats “six years” for sowing and pruning; BSB gives the duration once for both.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “the Sabbath of the land” will be food; BSB explains it as “Whatever the land yields during the Sabbath year.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the horn twice and uses a singular command followed by a plural command; BSB names the horn once, replaces it with “it,” and does not mark the change in the number addressed.
The Hebrew repeats the returning verb separately for property and clan; BSB gives it once for both.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says to eat the produce “from the field”; BSB adds “only” and “directly.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew names the seller’s “neighbor” twice, includes “from the hand,” and calls the other person “his brother”; BSB replaces the second neighbor with “him,” omits the hand image, and says “each other.”
The Hebrew says years “after the Jubilee” and “years of harvests”; BSB adds “last” to the Jubilee and “remaining” to the harvest years.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew gives “do,” “keep,” and another “do them”; BSB compresses these to “keep” and “carefully observe.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew presents a question that the people may “say” and then “Behold, we shall not sow”; BSB uses inward “wonder” and turns the explanation into an “if” clause.
The Hebrew says “I will command My blessing” and leaves the following crop-producing subject unnamed; BSB says “send My blessing” and explicitly supplies “the land.”
The Hebrew repeats eating and the old produce at the end; BSB expresses that eating once.
The Hebrew repeats “the land” in “for the land is Mine”; BSB uses “it.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew expresses prosperity as “his hand reaches”; BSB says “he prospers.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the images “his hand has not found enough” and the property remaining “in the hand” of the buyer; BSB uses “he cannot obtain enough” and “in possession.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the house will belong to the buyer “for his generations”; BSB says “to its buyer and his descendants.”
